description: We are first-year B.Tech CSE students building smart solutions using Python, machine learning, and data science. For this challenge, we developed "Harmonization of Modis & VIIRS Hot Spots" to help farmers. Looking for passionate teammates!
summary: Project Alpha Group developed an advanced multi-sensor wildfire anomaly harmonisation and machine learning platform to address critical discrepancies between NASA's MODIS (Collection 6.1) and VIIRS (Collection 2) thermal hotspot datasets. By aligning data schemas, mapping confidence levels to a uniform integer scale, scaling VIIRS Fire Radiative Power (FRP) by 1.15x, and eliminating duplicate detections across a 1km coordinate grid, our pipeline successfully processed 10,000 raw detections down to 7,603 reliable harmonised events. Furthermore, we trained a robust 150-estimator Random Forest Regressor on features like brightness, spatial coordinates, time of day, and confidence levels, achieving an impressive R² score of 0.778 for predictive FRP estimation. Integrated into an interactive Streamlit and PyDeck geospatial web application, Project Alpha Group empowers emergency responders and researchers with real-time multi-satellite visualization, filtering, and comparative analytics to enhance global wildfire monitoring and disaster management.
details:
Project Alpha Group is an end-to-end machine learning-powered geospatial web application designed to harmonize satellite fire hotspot datasets from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS sensors. Operating through an interactive Streamlit dashboard, the system ingests raw global CSV datasets (MODIS_C6_1_Global_24h.csv and J1_VIIRS_C2_Global_24h.csv) and performs automated data cleaning and feature engineering. It standardizes brightness temperatures, calibrates Fire Radiative Power (FRP x1.15 for VIIRS), maps confidence levels into a uniform scale ($0–2$), and converts acquisition dates and times into unified datetime objects. To eliminate spatial redundancy caused by overlapping sensor swaths, the pipeline applies a 1km grid-based spatial deduplication algorithm, retaining the highest-confidence observations. Furthermore, it trains a robust RandomForestRegressor ($150$ estimators) to predict and analyze calibrated FRP with high accuracy ($R^2 \approx 0.778$), visualized dynamically via Pydeck scatterplot maps and interactive scatter charts.

  • Tools, Coding Languages & Software:
    • Language: Python
    • Core Libraries & Frameworks: Streamlit (for web UI), Pandas & NumPy (for data wrangling and transformation), Pydeck (for spatial geospatial rendering), and Scikit-Learn (for RandomForestRegressor, train_test_split, and metric evaluation).
  • Benefits & Intended Impact:
    Fire management agencies and researchers often struggle with discrepancies when combining multi-sensor satellite observations due to differing resolutions, calibration biases, and overlapping detections. Project Alpha Group bridges this gap by automatically removing duplicates and normalizing fire radiative power. This provides emergency responders, environmental researchers, and agricultural authorities with a clean, unified, and reliable real-time situational awareness tool for wildfire monitoring and disaster management.
  • Creativity & Team Considerations:
    Our solution introduces a streamlined workflow that transforms complex, disparate satellite feeds into a seamless, low-latency web interface that processes thousands of detections in seconds. By balancing rigorous machine learning prediction with intuitive geospatial visualization and clear metric readouts (Total Detections: 10,00010,00010,000, Post-Harmonisation: 7,6037,6037,603, Duplicates Removed: 2,3972,3972,397, and R2:0.778R^2: 0.778R2:0.778), Alpha Group delivers an accessible, high-performance tool ready for real-world deployment.
